chunks: It is narrated from Al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah that he said:
Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ruled that whatever the judges err in regarding bloodshed or amputation, it is upon the public treasury of the Muslims.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the title of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام
key_terms.الْقُضَاةُ: judges entrusted with issuing legal rulings
key_terms.بَيْتِ مَالِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the public treasury from which communal financial liabilities are paid
key_terms.دَمٍ: a case involving bloodshed or unlawful killing
key_terms.قَطْعٍ: a case involving cutting or bodily amputation

ai.seo_question: Who bears financial liability when judges make a mistaken ruling in cases of bloodshed or amputation in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling from أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام concerning judicial error in severe cases involving bloodshed or bodily amputation. It establishes that liability for such mistaken judicial decisions is borne by the Bayt al-Mal of the Muslims, reflecting institutional responsibility within the justice system.
